questions.question: What did the President order on 20 January, and on what authority?
How far did the federal workforce shrink, and through what instruments?
How was the Alien Enemies Act used, and how did the courts respond?
Where and under what authority were troops deployed in American cities, and what did courts decide?
What checks did courts and Congress apply?
How were pardons and protest part of the year?

findings.finding: Executive Order 14158 (20 January 2025) renamed the US Digital Service the US DOGE Service and created a temporary organization within it to run until 4 July 2026.
findings.quotation: The U.S. DOGE Service Temporary Organization shall terminate on July 4, 2026.

findings.finding: Executive Order 14160 (20 January 2025) directed agencies not to recognize the citizenship of children born in the United States to mothers unlawfully or temporarily present whose fathers were not citizens or permanent residents, for births more than 30 days after the order.
findings.quotation: when that person's mother was unlawfully present in the United States

findings.finding: Proclamation 10887 (20 January 2025) commuted the sentences of 14 named people and granted a full, complete and unconditional pardon to all others convicted of offences related to the events at the Capitol on 6 January 2021.
findings.quotation: grant a full, complete and unconditional pardon to all other individuals convicted of offenses related to events that occurred at or near the United States Capitol

findings.finding: Proclamation 10903 (14 March 2025) declared that Venezuelan citizens aged 14 or older who were members of Tren de Aragua and not naturalized or permanent residents were liable to be apprehended and removed as alien enemies under the Alien Enemies Act.
findings.quotation: 14 years of age or older

findings.finding: On 7 April 2025 the Supreme Court held that detainees challenging removal under the Alien Enemies Act must proceed in habeas in the district of confinement, and that they are entitled to notice and an opportunity to seek habeas relief.
findings.quotation: the detainees are entitled to notice and opportunity to be heard

findings.finding: On 10 April 2025 the Supreme Court left in place, with clarification, a district court order that the Government "facilitate" the release of Kilmar Abrego Garcia from custody in El Salvador and ensure his case is handled as it would have been had he not been improperly sent there.
findings.quotation: The order properly requires the Government to "facilitate" Abrego Garcia's release from custody in El Salvador

findings.finding: On 27 June 2025, in Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court held 6-3 (Barrett for Roberts, Thomas, Alito, Gorsuch and Kavanaugh) that universal injunctions likely exceed the equitable authority Congress has given federal courts, and partly stayed injunctions against the birthright citizenship order without deciding its merits. The applications did not raise, and the Court did not address, whether the order violates the Citizenship Clause or the Nationality Act.
findings.quotation: Universal injunctions likely exceed the equitable authority that Congress has given to federal courts.

findings.finding: The memorandum of 7 June 2025 called at least 2,000 National Guard members into federal service under 10 U.S.C. 12406 for 60 days to protect ICE and other federal personnel and property.
findings.quotation: at least 2,000 National Guard personnel and the duration of duty shall be for 60 days

findings.finding: The Ninth Circuit (19 June 2025) recorded that the President had ordered 4,000 Guard members into federal service under section 12406 on 7 June, and stayed Judge Charles Breyer's order returning control of the Guard to California.
findings.quotation: to order 4,000 members of the National Guard into federal service for 60 days

findings.finding: Executive Order 14333 (11 August 2025) declared a crime emergency in the District of Columbia and, under section 740 of the Home Rule Act, directed the Mayor to provide the services of the Metropolitan Police Department for federal purposes.
findings.quotation: section 740 of the District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act

findings.finding: On 23 December 2025 the Supreme Court denied the Government's application to deploy 300 federalized Illinois National Guard members, reading "regular forces" in section 12406(3) to refer to the military; Justices Alito, Thomas and Gorsuch dissented.
findings.quotation: The application for stay is denied.

findings.finding: Public Law 119-21, an act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14, was approved on 4 July 2025.
Public Law 119-37, approved 12 November 2025, provided continuing appropriations through 30 January 2026 together with three full-year appropriations acts.

CRS records that a government-wide funding gap occurred at the beginning of fiscal 2026 (which begins on 1 October) and lasted 42 full days, ending when Public Law 119-37 was enacted on 12 November 2025; the previous longest, in fiscal 2019, lasted 34 full days, and since fiscal 1977 gaps have ranged from 1 day to 42 full days. (The CRS text misprints the end year as 2015.) The fiscal 2019 gap began after funding expired on 21 December 2018 and ended on 25 January 2019.
findings.quotation: after lasting 42 full days

findings.finding: Public Law 119-38, the Epstein Files Transparency Act, approved 19 November 2025, required the Attorney General to make public within 30 days unclassified Justice Department records relating to Jeffrey Epstein.
findings.quotation: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act

findings.finding: The House passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act on 18 November 2025 by 427 votes to 1.
findings.quotation: Aye: 427 No: 1

findings.finding: Federal government employment was 3,010,000 in January 2025 and 2,722,000 in December 2025 (seasonally adjusted, thousands: 3010 and 2722), a fall of 288,000; the largest monthly fall was in October, from 2,914,000 to 2,748,000. The fall of 288,000 is nearly 300,000, or 9.6 per cent of the January level.

BLS reported that federal employment fell by 162,000 in October 2025 as employees who had accepted a deferred resignation offer left payrolls, and was down by 271,000 from its January peak by November.
findings.quotation: as some federal employees who accepted a deferred resignation offer came off federal payrolls

findings.finding: The President federalized 300 Illinois National Guard members on 4 October 2025 and Texas Guard members the next day; the district court barred deployment and the Seventh Circuit kept the bar. The Court held that "regular forces" in section 12406(3) likely means the regular military, so federalization requires authority to use the military to execute the laws, which the Posse Comitatus Act generally forbids, and the Government had identified none.
findings.quotation: We conclude that the term "regular forces" in §12406(3) likely refers to the regular forces of the United States military.

findings.finding: Individuals, organizations and States filed three suits to enjoin Executive Order 14160, and district courts issued universal injunctions barring its enforcement against anyone.
findings.quotation: filed three separate suits to enjoin the implementation and enforcement of President Trump's Executive Order No. 14160

findings.finding: Each agency head was to establish a DOGE Team of at least four employees within thirty days.
findings.quotation: a DOGE Team of at least four employees

findings.finding: On 15 March 2025 the United States removed Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia to El Salvador, where he was detained; it acknowledged that a withholding order forbade his removal there, that the removal was therefore illegal, and that it resulted from an "administrative error."
findings.quotation: the removal to El Salvador was therefore illegal

findings.finding: The district court found plaintiffs likely to succeed because none of the predicates to federalization under section 12406 existed and the order was not issued through the Governor.
findings.quotation: none of the predicates to federalization required under § 12406 existed

findings.finding: Justice Sotomayor dissented, joined by Justices Kagan and Jackson; Justice Jackson also filed a separate dissent.
findings.quotation: SOTOMAYOR, J., filed a dissenting opinion, in which KAGAN and JACKSON, JJ., joined. JACKSON, J., filed a dissenting opinion.
